producer_judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are Class X (rank 1) Indicators in the same Chapter 15 'Our Environment' under the Natural Resources Content Domain, but they sit on different parent paths: C238 under CLO104/LO1 (differentiating objects/phenomena, biodegradable vs non-biodegradable) and C246 under CLO105/LO3 (planning and conducting investigations about factors impacting ecosystems). The pair-specific substantive link is that the ability to classify wastes as biodegradable or non-biodegradable (C238) is the conceptual categorisation a learner applies when investigating how medical wastes are actually segregated and disposed at a health centre (C246); the investigative indicator extends the classification skill into a field inquiry about disposal practice, so proficiency in C238 supports success in C246. Same-rank direction is grounded in this classification-to-applied-investigation shift rather than on the shared Class, Chapter, LC 'waste' token overlap, or adjacent source pages, which alone would not establish a relation. Source evidence for both SFIs is truncated and both carry upstream merge/code audit context, so the judgment rests on the bounded indicator texts and hierarchy shown.
